sessions.summary: Both requests were carried out, nothing declined. The cheaper-summary improvement cherry-picked onto the migration tip with no conflict, so the history summary now runs on SUMMARY_MODEL (gpt-4o-mini by default, -93% on the measured sample) while chat and vision stay on OPENAI_MODEL. The plugin-result port was then plain-reverted, which put the bot's history back to its base-commit shape but left the plugin follow-up as a request Router answers 400 on, and that unpaired result also poisoned every later turn of the same conversation (1 valid, 3 invalid over the plugin driver); a second commit therefore teaches the vendored runtime to keep a request whose function result names no call in the same request on OpenAI, where that legacy shape is accepted, exactly as it already does for the image and audio calls. After both, chat (buffered and streamed), vision and summary still reach Router, 5 of 5 valid, the repo's suite is 5 passed as on the base commit, and check --final --tests is OK with one flag for the human: the vendored runtime was edited by hand.

results.note: Cherry-picked router-migrate/improve/cheap-summaries onto the current tip with no conflict; __summarise sends SUMMARY_MODEL (gpt-4o-mini, falling back to OPENAI_MODEL when unset) and the simulator and live Router both show the summary feature on gpt-4o-mini, 200.

Reverted the port, so a plugin result is recorded on its own again and the history is byte-for-byte the base-commit shape; because Router rejects that shape (400 on the follow-up and on every later turn of that conversation, 3 invalid requests), the follow-up commit keeps such requests on OpenAI via the runtime's existing untranslatable route, leaving 0 invalid and the other four Router calls untouched.

flags.detail: the vendored runtime was edited by hand
